in.answer_say: Went! Yesterday we went home.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai bentuk lampau: go jadi went.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “Yesterday I go to school.”? 😅 Untuk kejadian kemarin, pakai bentuk lampau: “Yesterday I went to school.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “went”. Ceritakan harimu kemarin dengan went, ate, saw. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian does not change verbs, but English uses the past form: go becomes went.
en.caption: Do you say “Yesterday I go to school.”? 😅 For yesterday, use the past form: “Yesterday I went to school.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Is! He is tall.

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “dia cantik” tanpa kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh is/am/are.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “She beautiful.”? 😅 Jangan lupa is setelah she: “She is beautiful.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “is”. Buat tiga kalimat pendek dengan is hari ini. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “dia cantik” has no verb, but English needs is, am or are.
en.caption: Do you say “She beautiful.”? 😅 Do not forget is after she: “She is beautiful.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Pens! I have three pens.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia tidak menambah akhiran jamak, tapi bahasa Inggris menambah -s setelah angka lebih dari satu.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I have two book.”? 😅 Dari dua ke atas, tambahkan s: “I have two books.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “pens”. Hitung benda di sekitarmu dan tambahkan s. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian has no plural ending, but English adds -s after a number above one.
en.caption: Do you say “I have two book.”? 😅 With two or more, add s: “I have two books.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Say very much at the end.
in.answer_say: Like! I like music very much.

native.tip: “Saya sangat suka” tidak bisa diterjemahkan kata per kata. Pakai like ... very much.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I very like coffee.”? 😅 Letakkan very much di akhir: “I like coffee very much.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “like”. Coba bilang “I like ... very much” untuk makananmu. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Saya sangat suka” cannot be translated word for word. Use like ... very much.
en.caption: Do you say “I very like coffee.”? 😅 Put very much at the end: “I like coffee very much.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Are! Where are you going?

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “Kamu mau ke mana?” cukup singkat, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh are dan going.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “Where you go?”? 😅 Tanyakan dengan lengkap: “Where are you going?”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “are”. Tanya temanmu: “Where are you going?” Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian the short question is fine, but English needs are and going.
en.caption: Do you say “Where you go?”? 😅 Ask the full question: “Where are you going?”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Ate! I already ate lunch.

native.tip: Kata “sudah” di bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai bentuk lampau: ate.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I already eat breakfast.”? 😅 Untuk yang sudah selesai, pakai ate: “I already ate breakfast.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “ate”. Bilang “I already ate” saat ditanya sudah makan. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian “sudah” does not change the verb, but English uses the past form: ate.
en.caption: Do you say “I already eat breakfast.”? 😅 For something done, use ate: “I already ate breakfast.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Is! My teacher is kind.

native.tip: Kita sering bilang “teman saya, dia baik”, tapi di bahasa Inggris subjek tidak diulang.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “My friend she is nice.”? 😅 Subjek cukup disebut sekali: “My friend is nice.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “is”. Ceritakan temanmu tanpa kata she tambahan. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: We often say “teman saya, dia baik”, but English does not repeat the subject.
en.caption: Do you say “My friend she is nice.”? 😅 Say the subject only once: “My friend is nice.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Are! There are many cars.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia tidak membedakan tunggal dan jamak, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai there are untuk banyak benda.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “There is many people here.”? 😅 Untuk banyak, pakai there are: “There are many people here.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “are”. Lihat sekitarmu dan bilang “There are ...”. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian does not separate one and many, but English uses there are for many things.
en.caption: Do you say “There is many people here.”? 😅 For many, use there are: “There are many people here.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Bored! I am bored in class.

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “bosan” cuma satu kata, tapi bahasa Inggris beda: bored untuk perasaanmu, boring untuk hal yang membosankan.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I am boring today.”? 😅 Perasaanmu? Pakai bored: “I am bored today.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “bored”. Ingat: kamu bored, filmnya boring. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian has one word for it, but English differs: bored is your feeling, boring is the thing.
en.caption: Do you say “I am boring today.”? 😅 Your feeling? Use bored: “I am bored today.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Turn on! Please turn on the radio.

native.tip: Kita sering bilang “buka lampu”, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai turn on.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “Please open the light.”? 😅 Untuk lampu dan radio, pakai turn on: “Please turn on the light.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “turn on”. Nyalakan lampu sambil bilang “Turn on the light”. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: We often say “buka lampu”, but English uses turn on.
en.caption: Do you say “Please open the light.”? 😅 For lights and radio, use turn on: “Please turn on the light.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I go to home after work.
in.answer_say: Go! I go home at night.

native.tip: Kita bilang “pergi ke rumah”, tapi di bahasa Inggris home tidak pakai to.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I go to home after work.”? 😅 Dengan home, tidak perlu to: “I go home after work.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “go”. Ucapkan “I go home” lima kali. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: We say “pergi ke rumah”, but in English home takes no to.
en.caption: Do you say “I go to home after work.”? 😅 With home, you do not need to: “I go home after work.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Am! I am very hungry.

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “saya sangat capek” tanpa kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh am.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I very tired today.”? 😅 Jangan lupa am sebelum very: “I am very tired today.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “am”. Bilang “I am very ...” untuk perasaanmu. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “saya sangat capek” has no verb, but English needs am.
en.caption: Do you say “I very tired today.”? 😅 Do not forget am before very: “I am very tired today.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Slept! Last night I slept well.

native.tip: Kata kerja bahasa Indonesia tidak berubah menurut waktu, tapi bahasa Inggris berubah: sleep jadi slept.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “Yesterday I sleep late.”? 😅 Untuk semalam, pakai slept: “Yesterday I slept late.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “slept”. Ceritakan tidurmu semalam dengan slept. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian verbs do not change with time, but English does: sleep becomes slept.
en.caption: Do you say “Yesterday I sleep late.”? 😅 For last night, use slept: “Yesterday I slept late.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Studying! I am studying now.

native.tip: “Saya sedang belajar” butuh am dan -ing di bahasa Inggris, bukan hanya study.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I study English now.”? 😅 Untuk yang sedang terjadi, pakai am studying: “I am studying English now.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “studying”. Bilang apa yang sedang kamu lakukan sekarang. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Saya sedang belajar” needs am and -ing in English, not only study.
en.caption: Do you say “I study English now.”? 😅 For right now, use am studying: “I am studying English now.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Has! He has a big house.

native.tip: Kata kerja bahasa Indonesia sama untuk semua orang, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai has setelah she dan he.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “She have a new car.”? 😅 Setelah she atau he, pakai has: “She has a new car.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “has”. Ceritakan temanmu: “He has ...”. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian verbs stay the same for everyone, but English uses has after she and he.
en.caption: Do you say “She have a new car.”? 😅 After she or he, use has: “She has a new car.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Doesn't! She doesn't like tea.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja bantu, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai doesn't setelah he dan she.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “He don't like fish.”? 😅 Setelah he atau she, pakai doesn't: “He doesn't like fish.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “doesn't”. Bilang tiga hal yang temanmu tidak suka. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian does not change the helper word, but English uses doesn't after he and she.
en.caption: Do you say “He don't like fish.”? 😅 After he or she, use doesn't: “He doesn't like fish.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Old! I am 30 years old.

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “25 tahun” sudah cukup, tapi bahasa Inggris perlu years old.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I am 25 years.”? 😅 Untuk umur, tambahkan old: “I am 25 years old.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “old”. Sebutkan umurmu lengkap: “I am ... years old”. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “25 tahun” is enough, but English needs years old.
en.caption: Do you say “I am 25 years.”? 😅 For your age, add old: “I am 25 years old.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Live! I live in a small town.

native.tip: Banyak yang menambah am. Di bahasa Inggris, live sudah kata kerja.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I am live in Jakarta.”? 😅 Cukup bilang I live: “I live in Jakarta.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “live”. Perkenalkan tempat tinggalmu: “I live in ...”. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Many learners add am. In English, live is already a verb.
en.caption: Do you say “I am live in Jakarta.”? 😅 Just say I live: “I live in Jakarta.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Me and my friend are late.
in.right: My friend and I are late.
in.answer_say: I! My sister and I are home.

native.tip: Kita bilang “saya dan teman saya”, jadi mudah tertukar. Di bahasa Inggris, subjek pakai I dan taruh diri sendiri terakhir.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “Me and my friend are late.”? 😅 Sebagai subjek, pakai “My friend and I”: “My friend and I are late.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “I”. Bilang “My friend and I” saat bercerita. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: It is easy to mix up. In English, use I as the subject and put yourself last.
en.caption: Do you say “Me and my friend are late.”? 😅 As the subject, use “My friend and I”: “My friend and I are late.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Swim! I can swim well.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia pakai “bisa untuk”, jadi kita menambah to. Di bahasa Inggris, can langsung diikuti kata kerja.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I can to swim.”? 😅 Setelah can, langsung kata kerja: “I can swim.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “swim”. Bilang “I can ...” untuk tiga hal yang kamu bisa. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Because of “bisa untuk”, learners add to. In English, can goes straight to the verb.
en.caption: Do you say “I can to swim.”? 😅 After can, use the verb directly: “I can swim.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: To! I want to eat.

native.tip: “Mau pulang” tidak butuh kata penghubung, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh to setelah want.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I want go home.”? 😅 Setelah want, pakai to: “I want to go home.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “to”. Bilang “I want to ...” tiga kali hari ini. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Mau pulang” needs no linking word, but English needs to after want.
en.caption: Do you say “I want go home.”? 😅 After want, use to: “I want to go home.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Help! I will help you.

native.tip: Mirip “akan untuk”, tapi di bahasa Inggris will langsung diikuti kata kerja.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I will to go tomorrow.”? 😅 Setelah will, langsung kata kerja: “I will go tomorrow.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “help”. Bilang rencanamu besok: “I will ...”. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: It sounds like “akan untuk”, but in English will goes straight to the verb.
en.caption: Do you say “I will to go tomorrow.”? 😅 After will, use the verb directly: “I will go tomorrow.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Of! She is afraid of spiders.

native.tip: Kita bilang “takut dengan”, tapi di bahasa Inggris pakai afraid of.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I am afraid with dogs.”? 😅 Untuk rasa takut, pakai of: “I am afraid of dogs.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “of”. Hafalkan “afraid of” bersama benda yang kamu takuti. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: We may say “takut dengan”, but English uses afraid of.
en.caption: Do you say “I am afraid with dogs.”? 😅 For fear, use of: “I am afraid of dogs.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: At! He is good at English.

native.tip: Kita bilang “pandai dalam”, tapi di bahasa Inggris pakai good at.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I am good in English.”? 😅 Untuk keahlian, pakai at: “I am good at English.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “at”. Bilang “I am good at ...” untuk kemampuanmu. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: We say “pandai dalam”, but English uses good at.
en.caption: Do you say “I am good in English.”? 😅 For a skill, use at: “I am good at English.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: I am late because of traffic.
in.answer_say: Because of! I am late because of rain.

native.tip: “Karena macet” cukup satu kata di bahasa Indonesia, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai because of sebelum kata benda.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I am late because traffic.”? 😅 Sebelum kata benda, pakai because of: “I am late because of traffic.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “because of”. Ceritakan alasanmu terlambat dengan because of. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Karena macet” is one word in Indonesian, but English uses because of before a noun.
en.caption: Do you say “I am late because traffic.”? 😅 Before a noun, use because of: “I am late because of traffic.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: I forgot to bring my book.
in.answer_say: To! Do not forget to call me.

native.tip: Di bahasa Indonesia “lupa bawa” langsung dua kata, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai to sebelum kata kerja kedua.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I forgot bring my book.”? 😅 Setelah forgot, pakai to: “I forgot to bring my book.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “to”. Bilang “I forgot to ...” untuk hal yang kamu lupa. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “lupa bawa” goes straight on, but English uses to before the second verb.
en.caption: Do you say “I forgot bring my book.”? 😅 After forgot, use to: “I forgot to bring my book.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I go to office by bus.
in.right: I go to the office by bus.
in.answer_say: The! She is at the market.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia tidak punya kata the, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh the sebelum tempat tertentu.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I go to office by bus.”? 😅 Sebelum tempat tertentu, pakai the: “I go to the office by bus.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “the”. Ceritakan perjalananmu: “I go to the ...”. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian has no word like the, but English needs the before a specific place.
en.caption: Do you say “I go to office by bus.”? 😅 Before a specific place, use the: “I go to the office by bus.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Quickly! She speaks quickly now.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia memakai kata yang sama untuk “lancar”, tapi bahasa Inggris menambah -ly setelah kata kerja.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I speak English fluent.”? 😅 Setelah kata kerja, pakai fluently: “I speak English fluently.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “quickly”. Latih “I speak slowly” dulu, lalu fluently. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian uses one word for “lancar”, but English adds -ly after a verb.
en.caption: Do you say “I speak English fluent.”? 😅 After a verb, use fluently: “I speak English fluently.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: Can you, not do you can!
in.answer_say: Can you! Can you speak English?

native.tip: “Apakah kamu bisa” tampak cocok dengan do you can, tapi di bahasa Inggris can sendiri yang dipindah ke depan.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “Do you can speak English?”? 😅 Untuk bertanya bisa, mulai dengan can: “Can you speak English?”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “Can you”. Tanya temanmu: “Can you ...?” Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Apakah kamu bisa” seems to fit do you can, but English moves can to the front by itself.
en.caption: Do you say “Do you can speak English?”? 😅 To ask about ability, start with can: “Can you speak English?”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Do! I do not know.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia cukup “tidak mengerti”, jadi orang menambah am. Di bahasa Inggris pakai do not.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I am not understand.”? 😅 Untuk menyangkal kata kerja, pakai do not: “I do not understand.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “do”. Latih “I do not understand” dengan tenang. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian says “tidak mengerti”, so learners add am. English uses do not.
en.caption: Do you say “I am not understand.”? 😅 To deny a verb, use do not: “I do not understand.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: Cheaper! My bag is cheaper.

native.tip: “Lebih murah” jadi more cheaper, padahal -er sudah berarti lebih.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “This bag is more cheaper.”? 😅 Pilih satu: cheaper, tanpa more: “This bag is cheaper.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “cheaper”. Bandingkan dua barang dengan -er. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: “Lebih murah” turns into more cheaper, but -er already means more.
en.caption: Do you say “This bag is more cheaper.”? 😅 Pick one: cheaper, no more: “This bag is cheaper.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: To listen to! I like to listen to music.

native.tip: “Suka main” langsung dua kata di bahasa Indonesia, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh to setelah like.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I like play football.”? 😅 Setelah like, pakai to: “I like to play football.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “to listen to”. Bilang “I like to ...” untuk hobimu. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: In Indonesian “suka main” goes straight on, but English needs to after like.
en.caption: Do you say “I like play football.”? 😅 After like, use to: “I like to play football.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.answer_say: For! I wait for the bus.

native.tip: Kita bilang “menunggu kamu”, tapi bahasa Inggris pakai wait for.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “I am waiting you.”? 😅 Setelah wait, pakai for: “I am waiting for you.”. Dengarkan Kak Ama, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “for”. Bilang “I am waiting for ...” ke temanmu. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: We say “menunggu kamu”, but English uses wait for.
en.caption: Do you say “I am waiting you.”? 😅 After wait, use for: “I am waiting for you.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: My mother is a nurse. He works hard.
in.right: My mother is a nurse. She works hard.
in.answer_say: He! My father is tall. He is 40.

native.tip: Bahasa Indonesia pakai “dia” untuk semua, tapi bahasa Inggris membedakan he dan she.
native.caption: Kamu sering bilang “My mother is a nurse. He works hard.”? 😅 Pria: he. Wanita: she: “My mother is a nurse. She works hard.”. Dengarkan Kak Carlos, lalu ulangi! Latihan lagi di app Lexkite.
native.comment: Jawaban: “He”. Ceritakan keluargamu dengan he dan she yang tepat. Latihan gratis lebih banyak di sini: {link}

en.tip: Indonesian uses “dia” for everyone, but English separates he and she.
en.caption: Do you say “My mother is a nurse. He works hard.”? 😅 Man: he. Woman: she: “My mother is a nurse. She works hard.”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
